summary: Android segmented-control content is shifted down and slightly right compared with React: the segment row starts around 2 px lower, and the first segment begins several pixels farther right.
Android selected segment has a much heavier shadow/offset than React. React shows a subtle bottom/right hard shadow, while Android shows a thicker black shadow that extends farther down and right.
Android selected segment fill appears slightly more saturated/deeper yellow than React, and the text/background contrast differs inside the selected state.

Android segment labels render smaller/lighter, especially the count text. In React, labels and counts read as more consistently dark and bold; in Android, counts such as "24" and "9" are lighter gray and visually recessed.
Android segment sizing and internal padding differ: segment boxes appear a little taller/heavier in border treatment, and text sits with different vertical centering than React.
likelyCauses: Android shared segmented-control component is using different text style tokens from React, likely font size/weight and secondary count color.
Selected-state shadow constants differ between Android and React, with Android using a larger hard-shadow offset or thicker duplicate layer.
Android selected background token may not match the React yellow token exactly.
Manual Android crop/component positioning or container padding differs from React element bounds, causing the row alignment offset.
cases.suggestedOwner: Shared UI / Android Compose segmented-control owner
suggestedFixes: Align Android segmented-control typography to the React component: label/count font size, weight, and count color for selected and unselected states.
Reduce Android selected-segment hard shadow offset/thickness to match React’s subtle bottom/right shadow.
Use the exact shared yellow token for the selected segment fill and verify disabled/secondary text colors do not alter count contrast unexpectedly.
Normalize segment row placement and outer padding so the first segment and row baseline match the React component bounds within the 342x96 capture.
Re-run the visual test for `components.ui.segmented-control.states` and compare both pixel mismatch and visual row alignment after token changes.
